the classical network structures (ResNet, Inception, DenseNet) work differently and can be used as the backbone of graph CNNs, which are more effective and efficient than existing state-of-the-art methods.

(1) the proposed G ResNet and G Inception outperform G DenseNet on most datasets; (2) the performance of graph recognition is highly dependent on the network structures, which is consistent with the results in image recognition; (3) the proposed G Inception achieves the best performance on most datasets, which is comparable to the performance of the state-of-the-art spectral graph CNN methods.

1) The basic network structures (e.g. Inception, Dense, ResNet) can be transformed into graph CNNs, and 2) These different network structures work differently on graph CNN, and the choice of network architectures should be determined by the graph datasets.

the following three main contributions: 1) We give a comprehensive analysis and review on the general graph CNN, especially in its graph spectral filtering operation; 2) We construct the classical network structures of ResNet and Inception into graph CNN, and introduce the DenseNet into the graph CNN for the first time; 3) We conduct extensive experiments on several public datasets to demonstrate the effectiveness of different network structures in graph recognition task.

the classical network structures are also effective in graph CNN, and it is important to choose the appropriate network framework according to the graph data characteristics.
the network structures are more important for graph CNNs than the network architectures.
